meta.source: Compiled from NBAGR (National Bureau of Animal Genetic Resources) registered-breed records, ICAR breed descriptors and regional livestock surveys.
meta.disclaimer: Milk yields are per-lactation averages reported in literature; individual animals vary widely with feed, management and parity. Entries marked 'landrace' are locally recognised populations whose formal descriptor documentation is limited.

breeds.name: Gir
breeds.coat: Shining red to red-and-white speckled; some animals almost white
breeds.horns: Long, curving backwards then forwards in a distinctive half-moon
traits: Pendulous dewlap and long drooping ears
breeds.summary: The flagship dairy breed of India, originating in the Gir forests of Saurashtra. Gir cattle are exported worldwide — most famously to Brazil, where they anchor a multi-billion dollar dairy industry.
breeds.fun_fact: Gir bulls founded the Brazilian 'Gir Leiteiro' line, which today produces more milk per animal than the breed's Indian homeland herd.

breeds.name: Sahiwal
breeds.coat: Reddish-dun to pale red, occasionally white patches on neck and brisket
breeds.horns: Short, stumpy and thick at the base
traits: Best tropical dairy cattle for heat tolerance
Strong resistance to ticks and internal parasites
Used to upgrade dairy herds across Africa and Australia
breeds.summary: Often called the best of the indigenous milch breeds, Sahiwal combines respectable yield with exceptional hardiness in hot, tick-infested climates.
breeds.fun_fact: Australian and Kenyan dairy programs crossed Sahiwal with Holstein-Friesian to create heat-tolerant composite breeds such as the Australian Milking Zebu.

breeds.name: Dangi
breeds.coat: Distinct white coat with irregular red or brown spots
breeds.horns: Medium, curved upwards and slightly inward
traits: Sure-footed draught animal on wet slopes
Secretes an oily substance from skin that protects against rain
breeds.summary: A hardy hill cattle breed from the Sahyadri ranges, prized for draught work in the wet, undulating terrain of the Dang district.
breeds.fun_fact: Dangi cattle skin exudes an oily secretion believed to waterproof the coat — a rare adaptation among Indian cattle to monsoon climates.

breeds.name: Khanostery
breeds.coat: Grey to brown, occasionally pied
traits: Valued as draught and manure source
breeds.summary: A locally recognised hill landrace maintained by smallholder and pastoral communities; formal descriptor documentation is limited.
breeds.fun_fact: Hill landraces like Khanostery are genetic reservoirs of altitude and cold tolerance traits.

breeds.name: Khillar
breeds.coat: White or grey; males often grey over the neck and hump
breeds.horns: Short, thick, emerging sideways then curving forward
traits: Bullocks prized for heavy cart work
breeds.summary: A classic Deccan draught breed whose bullocks are legendary for speed and endurance under the yoke on the black-cotton-soil plateau.
breeds.fun_fact: Khillar bullocks were historically preferred for long-distance carting between Deccan market towns, covering 40+ km a day.

breeds.name: Mehsana
breeds.coat: Black or grey-black, often with white markings on face, legs and tail tip
traits: Believed to be a Murrah × Surti cross
breeds.summary: A dependable dual-purpose buffalo from north Gujarat, combining Murrah milking ability with Surti hardiness; a mainstay of dairy cooperatives.
breeds.fun_fact: Mehsana buffaloes are among the longest-lactating Indian buffaloes, with lactations routinely exceeding 300 days.

breeds.name: Surti
breeds.coat: Rusty black to dark brown; two characteristic white bands ('chevrons') around the barrel
breeds.horns: Long, flat and sickle-shaped, curving backwards
traits: Very high milk fat — up to 12%
breeds.summary: A compact riverine buffalo from south Gujarat famous for extremely rich, high-fat milk — ideal for ghee and premium dairy products.
breeds.fun_fact: Surti milk fat can reach 12%, nearly triple that of typical dairy cattle, making it the 'cream' of Indian buffalo breeds.

breeds.name: Jaffarabadi
breeds.coat: Deep black, occasionally copper-toned
breeds.horns: Heavy, emerging downward then curving up in a ring-like shape
breeds.summary: The giant of Indian buffaloes, bred in the coastal tracts of Saurashtra; heavy-bodied, high-fat milchers maintained largely by traditional herders.
breeds.fun_fact: Adult Jaffarabadi bulls can exceed 900 kg, making them the heaviest riverine buffalo in India.

breeds.name: Banni
breeds.coat: Black to grey-black, occasionally white patches
traits: Grazes saline Banni grasslands at night
Recognised as a distinct breed in 2011
breeds.summary: A recently recognised, exceptionally resilient buffalo of the Kutch salt marshes, maintained by nomadic Maldhari herders on sparse, saline forage.
breeds.fun_fact: Banni buffaloes graze almost entirely at night across the salt-affected Banni grassland — a behaviour unique among Indian buffalo breeds.

breeds.name: Murrah
breeds.coat: Jet black, with white switch on tail; occasionally dark brown
breeds.horns: Short, tightly curled in a characteristic spiral
traits: Tightly curled horns are the breed hallmark
Used globally to upgrade buffalo herds
Strong feed conversion on green fodder
breeds.summary: The world's most influential riverine dairy buffalo, originating in Haryana; Murrah genetics underpin buffalo improvement programs from Brazil to the Philippines.
breeds.fun_fact: The record-holding Murrah bull 'Sultan' lineage semen has been exported to over 30 countries for buffalo improvement.

breeds.name: Nagpuri
breeds.coat: Black, sometimes deep brown with white facial streaks
breeds.horns: Long, flat and curved, sweeping backwards beside the neck
breeds.summary: The buffalo of the Vidarbha plains, recognised by its long, flat, backward-swept horns and ability to work and milk in harsh heat.
breeds.fun_fact: Nagpuri horn length can exceed one metre tip-to-tip, among the longest of any Indian buffalo.

breeds.name: Paras
breeds.coat: Grey-brown to fawn
breeds.summary: A locally recognised dual-purpose landrace; formal national descriptor documentation is limited and herds are maintained by regional farming communities.
breeds.fun_fact: Landrace populations such as Paras preserve allele diversity that registered breeds have narrowed.

breeds.name: Harnal
breeds.coat: Grey-white, darker in males
breeds.horns: Medium, springing outward and curving up
traits: Bullocks used for carting and ploughing
breeds.summary: A Deccan plateau landrace valued chiefly for draught bullocks, with cows contributing household milk under extensive management.
breeds.fun_fact: Deccan draught landraces historically moved with seasonal crop cycles across plateau districts.

breeds.name: Deoni
breeds.coat: Black-and-white spotted; the 'Balankya' complete-white pattern is prized
traits: Dual purpose with good draught bullocks
breeds.summary: A spotted dual-purpose breed of the Deccan, known for patterned coats and reliable bullocks for medium-farm draught work.
breeds.fun_fact: Deoni coat patterns have local names — a fully white animal is called 'Balankya' and commands premium prices at fairs.

breeds.name: Tharparkar
breeds.coat: White to grey, deepening on the neck in males
traits: Also called White Sindhi or Gray Sindhi
Survives extreme desert heat and drought
Good milker for a drought breed
breeds.summary: The desert cattle of the Thar, combining genuine milking ability with unmatched drought endurance — a lifeline breed for arid-zone pastoralists.
breeds.fun_fact: Tharparkar herds trek across the Thar with nomadic herders, surviving on sparse scrub that would starve most dairy breeds.

breeds.name: Red Sindhi
breeds.coat: Deep reddish-brown to dark red, darker in males
traits: Also called Red Karachi or Sindhi
breeds.summary: A richly coloured tropical dairy breed from Sindh, exported for decades to upgrade hot-climate dairy herds across Asia, Africa and the Americas.
breeds.fun_fact: Red Sindhi genetics contributed to the Jamaican 'Jamaica Hope' composite, bred specifically for tropical dairy farming.

breeds.name: Hariana
breeds.coat: White to grey; males grey over neck and hump
traits: Premier draught bullocks of north India
Thrives on crop residues and fodder
Grey shading intensifies in working males
One of the oldest described Indian breeds
breeds.summary: The classic dual-purpose cattle of the Haryana plains, whose bullocks have pulled India's farm carts for centuries while cows supply household milk.
breeds.fun_fact: Hariana bullocks were the workhorses of Punjab canal-colony agriculture, prized for stamina in heavy clay soils.

breeds.name: Bvill
breeds.coat: Fawn to grey-brown
breeds.summary: A locally recognised landrace population; formal descriptor records are limited, and the type is preserved mainly through community herds.
breeds.fun_fact: Many Indian landraces remain undocumented genetically — each is a living library of local adaptation.

breeds.name: Purnathadi
breeds.coat: White-grey with darker shading on males
traits: Named for the Purna river basin
Adapted to black-cotton soils of Vidarbha
breeds.summary: Cattle of the Purna river valley in Vidarbha, maintained for draught power on the region's heavy black cotton soils.
breeds.fun_fact: River-basin landraces like Purnathadi are often named after the watercourse whose floodplains they graze.

breeds.name: Goa
breeds.coat: Reddish-brown to pied, varying by locality
breeds.summary: Coastal Konkan cattle of Goa, kept in small herds for milk, draught and cultural purposes under high-rainfall conditions.
breeds.fun_fact: Goan cattle feature prominently in village 'zatra' (fair) processions along the Konkan coast.

breeds.name: Sona
breeds.coat: Light fawn to golden-white ('sona' = golden)
traits: Dual purpose milk and light draught
breeds.summary: A golden-coated riverine landrace of the eastern lowlands, maintained for household milk and light farm work.
breeds.fun_fact: The name 'Sona' (gold) refers to the breed's characteristic warm golden coat in sunlight.

breeds.name: Khargvi
breeds.coat: Grey-brown, occasionally pied
breeds.summary: A pastoral landrace kept by migratory herding communities, adapted to long seasonal movements between grazing grounds.
breeds.fun_fact: Pastoral landraces cover hundreds of kilometres a year on traditional migration routes.

breeds.name: Bhagnari
breeds.coat: White to light grey, deep shading on neck in males
breeds.horns: Medium, thick at base, curving upwards
breeds.summary: A heavyweight draught breed of the Nara valley, producing some of the largest and most powerful bullocks in South Asia.
breeds.fun_fact: Bhagnari bullocks are so prized for heavy carting that a single pair can out-pull a small tractor on soft ground, say herders.

breeds.name: Lakhori
breeds.coat: Fawn to reddish-brown
breeds.summary: A locally recognised landrace maintained in regional herds; formal descriptor documentation is limited.
breeds.fun_fact: Community-maintained landraces often carry unique disease-resistance traits lost in commercial breeds.

breeds.name: Mursali
breeds.coat: Brown to grey-brown
breeds.summary: A locally recognised landrace preserved by regional farming communities; formal documentation remains limited.
breeds.fun_fact: Documenting landraces like Mursali is a race against time as herds shrink each decade.

breeds.name: Kadakathri
breeds.coat: Dark brown to grey
breeds.summary: A locally recognised landrace with limited formal documentation, maintained by traditional herding communities.
breeds.fun_fact: The name evokes the breed's spirited ('kadak') character, prized in working bullocks.
